subject: Clarify: LLM training eligibility and prompt/response retention
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@fintechco.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: privacyops@fintechco.com
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: LLM training on customer prompts — quick clarification

Diego —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our Privacy Ops team has two short questions related to how Redwood handles prompts and responses in hosted inference:

1) Do customer prompts/responses get used to train or improve Redwood models by default? If yes, is there an opt-out?
2) What is your retention policy for raw prompts and generated responses (both short-term logs and longer-term storage used for analytics)?

We need short, actionable answers and any supporting artifacts (DPA clause references, retention matrix, or an architecture diagram) to include in our SIG questionnaire. Can you also confirm whether exclusion for training is supported per-tenant or only globally?

Appreciate a reply by end of week — we have a scheduled SIG review next Tuesday.

Best,
Lisa Chen\Privacy & Risk\FinTechCo

----
Attachment: fintech-qa-llm.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)

From: diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@fintechco.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-10-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: LLM training on customer prompts — quick clarification

Lisa —

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front:

• No, customer prompts/responses are NOT used to train Redwood hosted models by default.
• Yes, customers can opt-in to allow their data to be included in improvement pipelines; opt-out is the default for hosted accounts unless the customer explicitly enables data contribution.
• Exclusion (training opt-out) is supported per-tenant and enforced at the ingestion layer — we do not mix opt-out traffic with contribution queues.
• Retention: short-term request logs (used for routing/debugging) are kept 30 days by default; full prompt/response traces kept for debugging/quality may be retained up to 90 days unless the tenant requests shorter retention in their contract. Long-term analytics aggregates (token counts, latencies) are stored in anonymized form indefinitely for capacity planning.

I attached: a simplified dataflow diagram and a one-page note on our training exclusion process. For SIG/DPA reference: section 4.2 of our DPA covers customer data usage and training opt-outs; I pulled the SOC 2 extract you asked about as well.

If it helps, we can provide a short statement your legal team can include in the SIG spreadsheet. We can also produce a tenant-specific evidence package (audit logs showing opt-out enforcement) if you need deeper proof.

Next steps:
1) Let me know if you want the tenant-specific audit export (we typically need a signed data request and the tenant ID).
2) If FinTechCo requires a retention shorter than 30 days for request logs, we can propose an addendum to the DPA and confirm feasibility with infra.

Best,
Diego Fernandez\Senior Solutions Architect\Redwood Inference\t

Summary (short):
- Default: No training on customer prompt/response content. Opt-out by default; per-tenant opt-in only.
- Retention: request logs 30 days default; full traces up to 90 days unless contractually shortened; aggregated metrics retained longer in anonymized form.
- Evidence: Dataflow diagram, training exclusion process doc, SOC 2 extract, and a Console screenshot showing the "Data Contribution" toggle.
